comment: CAM same-model preset, sweep 1 (the default first run): CAM is
tendency-driven, so physics_update -- the one subroutine through which
every parameterization's tendencies reach the state -- is a single
comparison point that covers all of physics, on every physics suite
(cam, cam7, simple) and across refactors. Each hit self-labels via
ptend%name (the producing parameterization) plus the call-site line.
Entry-state capture doubles as a physics/dynamics discriminator: if
state arrives already differing at the FIRST update of a step while
every ptend of the previous step matched, the divergence entered
between physics steps (dynamics/coupling) -- drill into the stepon_*/
dyn_run boundaries next (element_t capture: capture_se_dycore.json).
ptend is DEALLOCATED inside physics_update, so its exit bytes are
freed memory: the intents override compares it at entry only.
Known blind spot: pbuf fields (written via pbuf_get_field pointers)
and driver-local arrays (dlf, cmfmc, ...) bypass physics_update; a
divergence carried that way surfaces at the CONSUMING scheme's ptend,
one or more schemes late. For sharper input attribution run sweep 2:
targets_cam_anchors.json. Usage: dropsonde --base BASELINE_CASE
--test MODIFIED_CASE --targets targets_cam_update.json --source-root
$CAM/src [--launch 'mpiexec -n 1 {gdb} : -n N-1 {exe}']. Both cases
need the same PE layout, NTHRDS=1, DEBUG (-O0; on Izumi gnu >= 11
add -gdwarf-4 for gdb 8.2).
